Full-dose support for women facing hair loss, chronic stress, and the hormonal imbalance underneath it.

The words nobody gave you

Androgenetic alopecia. DHT.

It is the most common cause of hair loss in women, and most of us are never given the name for it.

Female pattern hair loss

Not another biotin supplement.

Most hair supplements are built around biotin and a handful of vitamins. They are made for hair that is thinning because something is missing from the diet. That is one cause — and in women, it is rarely the main one.

Female pattern hair loss — androgenetic alopecia — works differently. It comes down to how your follicles respond to androgens, and to DHT in particular: a hormone your body converts from testosterone. Follicles sensitive to it produce finer, shorter hairs with each cycle, until eventually they stop. It usually shows first at the parting and the temples, and it very often arrives alongside stress, hormonal shifts, or the years after a difficult period.

It affects an enormous number of women, and it remains strikingly under-researched compared with the same condition in men. Which is why so much of what is sold to us is a vitamin with good packaging.

Saede is formulated around those mechanisms instead: the androgen pathway, the cortisol and stress side, the hormonal and metabolic picture underneath, and the nutrients hair is actually built from — all at the amounts the research used.

We looked for a single product that did all of it for women, and we could not find one. So we are making it.

Not a general hair vitamin. A supplement made specifically for women living with female pattern hair loss. If this is what you have been searching for, you can stop looking.

Saede is a food supplement, formulated for women with androgenetic alopecia. It is support alongside proper medical care, not a replacement for it — androgenetic alopecia is a medical condition, so please see a doctor about it too.

I was coming out of the shower to my mother with my arms full of hair, sobbing. Look at this. I don't know what to do. I'm so scared.

Sonja, founder of Saede

My story

Saede is not a brand that found a gap in a market. It is one woman building the thing she spent years, and a great deal of money, trying to assemble for herself — because nobody would help her do it.

Nobody ever gave her the words androgenetic alopecia. Without them, she could not even search. It took a stranger on TikTok, at the end of her degree, to say the one thing every doctor had left out.

Three fronts, one system

Hair loss in women is rarely one problem. So Saede does not work on one thing.

The same formula works on all three at once, because in the body they were never separate to begin with.

The androgen pathway

Saw palmetto, pumpkin seed oil and nettle root, at the amounts used in the research — chosen for the DHT side of female pattern hair loss, which is where most hair supplements never go.

Stress and cortisol

Ashwagandha at 600 mg, the amount used in the research on cortisol. Stress is one of the three roots, and it is the one almost every hair supplement ignores entirely.

The hormonal and metabolic picture

Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol at 4 g in the 40:1 ratio: the most-researched nutritional ingredient in women with PCOS, studied for insulin sensitivity and blood sugar as well as hormonal balance.

How it works

Real results take time.

Hair grows on its own schedule, and the women who see a change are the ones who stay with it. Here is what that usually looks like.

Months 1 – 3

The quiet work

Your body starts filling in what it has been short of. The first thing most women notice is less hair in the brush and in the shower — a small change, but a real one, and usually the earliest sign that something is shifting.

Months 3 – 6

You start to see it

Around three months is when the first change usually shows: fine new hairs coming through along the parting and the hairline. They are soft and easy to miss at first — which is why it is worth taking a photo at the start, so you have something honest to compare against.

Month 6 and beyond

Fuller, and worth keeping

By six months there is usually something you can genuinely see, and something other people notice too. Staying with it is what protects it — the roots we are working on do not disappear, so neither does the support.

This is why Saede is built as a system rather than a single bottle.

Give it the full course. That is when it works, and it is the most useful thing we can tell you.

Questions

The things worth asking before you buy anything.

When does Saede actually launch?

We are not selling yet. The formula is with our manufacturer for technical and regulatory sign-off, and we are not going to start taking money before the testing is done and the doses are confirmed against EU limits.

We would rather be late than launch something we have to quietly water down. Leave your email on the launch list and we will write to you when it is ready — that is the only thing we will use it for.

How long before I see anything?

Most women notice the first changes around three months, with fuller results by six. Usually the first thing to change is not new growth — it is less hair in the shower drain and on the brush.

Hair grows slowly. It is biology, not marketing, and no supplement can move faster than a hair follicle. Anyone promising you results in three weeks is selling you something.

Why do you ask for three months minimum?

Because a single month does nothing measurable, and we would rather lose the sale than take your money for a bottle we know is too short to help.

Three months is the shortest honest course. It is also roughly when the hair growth cycle gives you something to actually look at. The women who stop at six weeks are the ones who conclude nothing works — and we have both been there.

If a recurring payment is the part you do not want, the three-month starter bundle is the same course paid once, with nothing to cancel.

Should I get my blood tested first?

If you can, yes — and we will keep saying it even though it means some of you will discover you need something other than us.

Ask for ferritin specifically, not just a standard haemoglobin check: ferritin shows your iron stores, and it is the one most often left off. Worth adding: full thyroid function, vitamin D, and — if you also have acne or irregular cycles — testosterone, DHEA-S and SHBG.

Ask for the actual numbers rather than the word 'normal'. A result at the very bottom of a range and one in the middle are different situations, and only one of them gets described to you differently.

Some causes of hair loss need diagnosis and medical treatment rather than a supplement. You deserve to know which one you are dealing with. We wrote a guide to what to ask for.

Is it safe?

Saede is a food supplement made in an EU facility to Good Manufacturing Practice standards, and every batch will be tested by an independent laboratory. Every dose is kept inside EU maximum permitted levels — the vitamin D, selenium and zinc all sit well under their legal ceilings, which is deliberate rather than incidental.

That said: safe in general is not the same as safe for you. If you are pregnant, trying to conceive, breastfeeding, taking any prescribed medication — particularly hormonal contraception, thyroid medication or anything affecting blood sugar — or if you have a diagnosed condition, talk to your doctor or pharmacist before you start. Bring the ingredient list with you. That is what it is published for.

The powder contains marine collagen, which is a fish allergen, so it is not suitable if you have a fish allergy and it is not vegan.

How does the membership work, and how do I cancel?

Your Saede arrives every 28 days. The membership runs for a minimum of three deliveries, because that is the shortest course that can honestly do anything, and this is stated clearly at checkout before you pay.

After those first three deliveries you can pause, reschedule or cancel at any time, from your account, in two clicks. No phone call, no form, no retention script, and no offer sitting between you and the button.

We wrote a whole page about how cancelling works so you can read it before you ever give us a card, rather than discovering it afterwards.

What actually makes Saede different?

The amounts, and the fact that we publish them. Most things in this category list good ingredients in quantities too small to matter, because a long label sells and a full dose costs more to make. Twenty ingredients, every amount on the site.

Saw palmetto at 320 mg. Pumpkin seed oil at 400 mg. Ashwagandha at 600 mg. Myo-inositol at 4 g. Those are the amounts used in the research, and they are written into our manufacturing specification so the formula stays what we say it is.

And honesty about the parts that are less flattering. Our ingredients page says openly where the research is still thin, and where a study was done in men rather than women.
